ownership.quote: Founded 2017 Headquarters San Francisco, California Country/Territory United States CEO Eric Simons

stage.quote: It raised a series B in January from VC outfits including Emergence Capital and GV (Google Ventures), which brought its total funding to $105 million and boosted it to a $700 million valuation.
stage.note: WebContainers is StackBlitz's core browser-runtime technology (product name webcontainers.io), not a separately funded entity; funding/stage reflect the parent company StackBlitz, Inc., maker of Bolt.new. Series A stage was skipped in name (seed in 2022 -> series B in 2025) per Forbes/Bloomberg reporting; no series A was found in press.

total_funding_usd.basis: Forbes company profile, citing the Jan 2025 Series B close
total_funding_usd.quote: which brought its total funding to $105 million and boosted it to a $700 million valuation

last_round.quote: The company is set to raise $83.5 million in a deal led by Emergence Capital and GV, formerly Google Ventures, said CEO Eric Simons. Madrona Venture Group, Conviction and Mantis are also participating.

revenue.quote: The company claims it reached $4 million in annualized revenue within four weeks of launching in October 2024.

note: WebContainers (webcontainers.io) is StackBlitz's in-browser Node.js/WebAssembly runtime technology, licensed commercially via StackBlitz's Enterprise plan; it is not an independently funded company. StackBlitz itself was 'on the verge of shuttering' before Bolt.new (launched Oct 2024, built on WebContainers) drove rapid growth and the Jan 2025 $83.5M Series B at a $700M valuation (Bloomberg/Forbes). Not a Y Combinator company (no YC profile found for StackBlitz). Prior seed round: $7.9M led by Greylock (2022, TechCrunch).
